_: V90Modem's lifecycle pair: six arguments, two embedded member
constructions, five allocations, six sub-constructor calls with thirteen
and fifteen arguments, and a destructor of six guarded arms.
ALMOST NOTHING HERE IS A WRONG VALUE.  The whole class of defect this
pair can carry is a PERMUTATION -- an argument landing in a neighbouring
slot, a guard reading the field beside the one it releases -- so most of
these move a pointer rather than change a number.  They are catchable
only because t_v90modemctor.cpp compares the CONTENTS of all six
allocations and not merely the six pointers to them: `&mappingParams`
and `&mappingParamsAlt` are stored in the modulator or the demodulator
and in no field of V90Modem at all, so a swap of the two is invisible to
any comparison that stops at the object.
TWO ARE CAUGHT ONLY BY THE TRANSCRIPT PASS and would survive every byte
comparison in the file.  The opening announcement chooses "Analog" or
"Digital" on the ARGUMENT, where the switch below it reloads the
MEMBER; the two readings agree on every value the object ends up
storing, so nothing in memory can tell them apart.  Same for the
destructor's `side > 1`, whose only effect is a line of text.
ONE THING IS DELIBERATELY NOT MUTATED, and it is want of an observable
rather than an oversight: `compMode`, the constructor's fifth argument.
It is forwarded to `V90Demodulator` as argument 14 and reaches nothing
but the equaliser's eleventh argument (t_v90demctor.cpp), and the
equaliser is a block the DEMODULATOR allocates -- one level below the
six this file's test compares.  Handing it a different value would
change a byte no comparison here can see.  t_v90demctor.cpp is where
that claim is made and it is made there against the equaliser's own
contents.

why: `~V90Parameters` IS A SINGLE `ret` IN THE BLOB.  Disassembled:
`ref__ZN13V90ParametersD1Ev` at 0x279f0 is `c3` and `D2` at 0x279e0 is
`c3`, both followed only by alignment padding.  So the call this removes
does nothing at all, whichever side runs it, and no observation of
memory or of the allocator can separate the two spellings.
The class earns that: src/pump/v90/V90Parameters.cpp's destructor has an
empty body and V90Parameters has no base and no member of class type, so
there is no sub-object destruction for the call to carry.
It is NOT code-identical and that is the reason to keep the source as it
is: compiled both ways, the pristine form emits `push 0x49b4(%ebx);
call _ZN13V90ParametersD1Ev` and the mutated form emits neither, and the
blob has the call.  Removing it would cost a second-tier match to buy
nothing.
label: dtor: the parameter block is released without being destroyed

why: `side = modemSide;` is executed before the switch, and NOTHING between
the two can change either: the four calls in between are handed `p` (a
fresh allocation), `modemParams` and `params`, and not one of them is
given `this`, so no callee can reach +0x49bc.  The two spellings
therefore select the same arm for every input, and no differential test
can separate them.
It is recorded rather than deleted because the object DOES distinguish
them and the distinction is written into the source: 0x195de reloads
`0x49bc(%esi)` rather than reusing the register it stored from, which is
what a read of the member compiles to and not what a read of the
argument does.  That is a second-tier claim -- `make similarity`'s, not
`make phase`'s -- and this entry is the note that the first tier cannot
reach it.
label: ctor: the switch is taken on the argument and not on the member
